builder_plan.scenario: An assistant chooses the wrong API or sends arguments your product cannot use.
builder_plan.change: Apply the proposed tool-selection or argument-generation change in a sandbox.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current agent with the same tool schemas and task budget.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Correct completed actions, invalid calls, retries, latency, and cost per completed task.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: MRFoundry: Knowledge-guided agent loops for end-to-end MRI research
summary: MRFoundry replaces ad-hoc prompting of general-purpose coding agents for MRI research tasks with a package of domain knowledge, tool integrations, project-local memory, and output checks. It costs integration effort with existing agent frameworks, dependency on third-party LLM APIs, and maintenance of domain guidance, with no direct GPU or training cost. It can fail on tasks outside its curated guidance, its Hard-task success rate remains below 45%, and gains depend on the underlying model and the quality of contributed domain knowledge.
rationale: The package is specific to MRI acquisition, reconstruction, and data conventions, so it falls outside the production work of a general AI/ML engineer unless that engineer builds MRI research tooling.
technique: Knowledge-guided agent loops for MRI workflows

claims.statement: MRFoundry replaces ad-hoc prompting of general-purpose coding agents for MRI research tasks with a package of domain knowledge, tool integrations, project-local memory, and output checks. It costs integration effort with existing agent frameworks, dependency on third-party LLM APIs, and maintenance of domain guidance, with no direct GPU or training cost. It can fail on tasks outside its curated guidance, its Hard-task success rate remains below 45%, and gains depend on the underlying model and the quality of contributed domain knowledge.
All-checks-passed completion rose from 67.5% to 78.3% on 240 Core benchmark pairs and from 36.6% to 44.8% on 134 Hard pairs when agents used MRFoundry.
